_meta: Four subjects, each measured five times. The measurements within a subject are correlated (they are the same subject), so they are NOT five independent data points — they are repeated looks at one unit. The naive analysis treats all 20 measurements as independent and computes the standard error as sd/sqrt(20). The correct analysis recognizes the independent units are the 4 SUBJECTS: it takes each subject's mean and computes the standard error of those 4 means as sd_of_means/sqrt(4). Because the naive N (20) is inflated, its standard error is too small, its confidence interval too narrow, and a difference from the reference value can look significant when it is not. reference is the value we test the grand mean against.
